Hi Marta,

Thanks again for the interest — excited to run the Redwood Inference demo with the Skylabs infra team. We proposed a couple of slots in the calendar invite but noticed Skylabs' cloud ops region will hit a DST cutover the weekend after next, so I want to be explicit about offsets to avoid any confusion when attendees accept from different timezones.

Proposed slots (as in the invite):
- Tue, May 4 — 10:00–10:45 PT (UTC-7) / 13:00–13:45 ET (UTC-4) / 19:00–19:45 CEST (UTC+2)
- Wed, May 5 — 16:00–16:45 PT (UTC-7) / 19:00–19:45 ET (UTC-4) / 01:00–01:45 IST (next day, UTC+5:30)

Quick asks: please confirm which slot works for your team and confirm preferred display (e.g., "10:00 PT / 13:00 ET / 19:00 CEST" vs explicit offsets like "10:00 PT (UTC-7)"). We find that including both the common abbreviation and the numeric offset in the calendar title avoids mis-scheduling across EU/APAC customers.

I've attached a one-page agenda and a simple timezone cheatsheet we use internally. If you prefer, we can send separate invites that show times only in the organizer's locale plus the UTC offset.

Thanks — cc'ing Ben (solutions engineer) and Aisha (AM) so they can join the scheduling thread and pick the right deck/tech pre-reqs.

Best,
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference

Hi Vivek — thanks for the clear note. We're available for Tue May 4 but want to be careful: our EU infra group is on CEST (UTC+2) currently, but some of our infra folks in the UK will interpret "BST" (British Summer Time) and others use local calendar settings. Also, our APAC engagement team (India) will likely join remotely — they prefer seeing IST explicit.

If you could send the confirmed slot with both the abbreviation and the UTC offset in the calendar title and description that would remove ambiguity. For example: "May 4, 10:00 PT (UTC-7) / 13:00 ET (UTC-4) / 19:00 CEST (UTC+2) / 22:30 IST (UTC+5:30)".

We also have a short internal requirement: please avoid times that fall within our maintenance window in EMEA on May 4 between 19:30–20:00 CEST — that would conflict with an automated failover test. The first slot you proposed (19:00–19:45 CEST) overlaps the start of that window by 30 minutes, so if we do May 4 we need to start at 18:45 CEST or move to the second slot on May 5.

Two options from our side:
1) May 4 at 18:45 CEST (UTC+2) — corresponds to 09:45 PT (UTC-7) / 12:45 ET (UTC-4) / 22:15 IST (UTC+5:30) — shorter lead time but avoids maintenance overlap.
2) May 5 at your second slot (16:00 PT / 19:00 ET) but note that for India attendees that becomes early morning May 6 (01:30 IST) and may reduce attendance.

I'll leave scheduling preference to Redwood — either is fine for us if you mark the invite with full offsets.

Cheers,
Marta Rossi
Product Ops, Skylabs
